bill.title: ABC Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: Streamlined administrative processes for Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP may affect how providers interact with patients' caregivers and handle eligibility documentation.
Changes to Medicare and Medicaid administrative processes could affect insurers participating in these programs and their coordination with caregivers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs federal agencies to review and simplify the paperwork and application processes for Medicare, Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program, and Social Security. The goal is to reduce the burden on family caregivers by eliminating duplicative forms and streamlining eligibility procedures across these programs. Agencies must gather input from caregivers and state organizations, make improvements, and report their progress to Congress.

bill.title: EMPOWER for Health Act
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects hospitals and health systems that employ medical personnel in underserved areas by making those positions more attractive through loan forgiveness.
Medical schools and higher education institutions are affected because the loan forgiveness program changes the financial calculus for students pursuing health professions degrees.
Federal loan guarantees and forgiveness programs affect the student loan market and the financial institutions that service these loans.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would establish a federal loan forgiveness program for health professionals who work in underserved areas. It appears to focus on reducing student debt for doctors, nurses, and other medical personnel who commit to practicing in communities that lack adequate healthcare access. The program would likely be administered through existing federal student loan mechanisms.

bill.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 461.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

industries.rationale: The bill directly funds research and development of drugs and therapies for ALS and neurodegenerative diseases, affecting pharmaceutical and biotech companies developing these treatments.
Clinical trial enrollment requirements and expanded access to investigational drugs may affect hospitals and health systems conducting ALS research and treatment.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal programs that support research and development of treatments for ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease) and similar neurodegenerative diseases. It requires the National Institutes of Health to track safety data more closely when awarding grants for experimental drug studies, and directs the Food and Drug Administration to publish five-year plans describing how it will help develop and approve treatments for these rare diseases. The bill also mandates reports evaluating the effectiveness of these grant programs.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to "National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska Integrated Activity Plan Record of Decision".

industries.rationale: The resolution would reopen approximately 48% of the National Petroleum Reserve to oil and gas leasing, directly expanding access for extraction companies.
The resolution removes wildlife and subsistence protections established in the 2022 plan, affecting conservation and indigenous-rights advocacy organizations.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would nullify a 2022 Bureau of Land Management plan that closed roughly 48% of the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska to oil and gas leasing in order to protect wildlife and subsistence resources. If enacted, the resolution would revert to a 2020 plan that allowed more of the reserve to be leased for oil and gas development. The reserve is an approximately 23-million-acre area on Alaska's North Slope.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to "Coastal Plain Oil and Gas Leasing Program Record of Decision".
bill.latestActionText: Indefinitely postponed by Senate by Unanimous Consent.

industries.rationale: The resolution directly affects oil and gas leasing rights and acreage availability in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge Coastal Plain.
Environmental and conservation organizations have direct stakes in decisions governing wildlife refuge land use and protection.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would overturn a December 2024 Bureau of Land Management decision that restricted oil and gas leasing in Alaska's Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. The 2024 rule made about 1.2 million acres unavailable for leasing while keeping the legally required minimum of 400,000 acres open. If this resolution passes, it would nullify that restriction and potentially allow the earlier 2020 decision—which opened all 1.6 million acres to leasing—to govern instead.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to "Central Yukon Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan".
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 181.

industries.rationale: Land-use restrictions in Alaska's Central Yukon planning area directly affect oil and gas exploration and extraction opportunities on federal lands.
Designations of critical environmental concern areas affect mineral extraction and mining access on the affected federal acreage.
Land-use designations can affect development rights and property values for adjacent or inholding parcels.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would nullify a Bureau of Land Management rule issued in November 2024 that governs how approximately 3.6 million acres of federal land in Alaska's Central Yukon area may be used. The BLM rule designated 21 areas as critical environmental concern or research natural areas. If enacted, the resolution would cancel that rule and restore the prior land-management plan for the region.

bill.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose duties on articles imported from Canada.
subjects: Presidents and presidential powers, Vice Presidents

industries.rationale: The resolution directly affects the 10% tariff on Canadian energy and energy resources.
The 25% tariff on most Canadian imports affects manufacturers who source materials, components, or finished goods from Canada.
Retailers importing consumer goods from Canada face the 25% tariff that this resolution would eliminate.
Agricultural products and food imports from Canada are subject to the 25% tariff.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would end the national emergency that President Trump declared on February 1, 2025, which imposed a 25% tariff on most goods imported from Canada and a 10% tariff on Canadian energy imports. Terminating the emergency would remove the legal basis for these additional duties on Canadian products.

bill.title: Small County PILT Parity Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 474.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects federal payments to county and local governments that host tax-exempt federal lands.
Counties with significant federal land often host mining operations on those lands, and changes to local revenue formulas may indirectly affect permitting and local fiscal capacity.
Federal lands in small counties frequently include oil, gas, or coal extraction sites, and local revenue changes may affect the fiscal environment for these operations.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would modify federal payments to local governments that contain tax-exempt federal land. Specifically, it appears to adjust the Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILT) formula for small counties, which compensates localities for property-tax revenue they cannot collect on federally owned land. Without access to the bill text, the precise nature of the change to the formula or eligibility criteria cannot be described.

industries.rationale: The program directly funds schools in rural counties containing federal land.
The program funds road construction and maintenance projects in affected counties.
Counties with federal land often have timber and mineral extraction activities that may be affected by resource advisory committee project decisions.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends a federal program that sends payments to rural counties containing national forests and other federal land. The money helps fund local schools, roads, and municipal services. The bill provides payments through fiscal year 2026, including back payments for 2024 and 2025, and allows counties and advisory committees to continue initiating projects through 2028.

districtAwards.description: STATE OF ALASKA RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM - DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: ALASKA’S RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM  ORGANIZATION NAME: STATE OF ALASKA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH   SUBRECIPIENTS/SUB-AWARDEES: A WIDE RANGE OF ENTITIES ACROSS ALASKA WILL PARTICIPATE AS FUNDING SUBRECIPIENTS, INCLUDING: HEALTH CARE DELIVERY ORGANIZATIONS; TRIBAL HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS; COMMUNITY-BASED ENTITIES; EDUCATION AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT INSTITUTIONS; TECHNOLOGY AND INNOVATION VENDORS; PROVIDER AND TRADE ASSOCIATIONS; CONSULTING AND PROFESSIONAL SERVICES FIRMS; AND STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS OR AUTHORITIES ENGAGED IN PUBLIC HEALTH, EDUCATION, OR EMERGENCY MEDICAL RESPONSE.   PROJECT GOALS:    1. PROMOTE LIFELONG HEALTH AND WELL-BEING FOR RURAL, REMOTE, AND FRONTIER ALASKANS.    2. BUILD SUSTAINABLE, OUTCOMES-DRIVEN HEALTH SYSTEMS.    3. DRIVE WORKFORCE AND TECHNOLOGY INNOVATION.    TOTAL BUDGET AMOUNT: $1,000,000,000.00    BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF FUND USAGE: ALASKA PROPOSES TO USE RHTP FUNDING TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY-LED AND REGIONALLY DESIGNED HEALTH SYSTEMS THAT PROVIDE ACCESS TO A FULL CONTINUUM OF CARE AS CLOSE TO ALASKANS’ HOMES AS POSSIBLE. THE FUNDS WILL BE AWARDED TO ENTITIES TO LAUNCH PROJECTS IN SUPPORT OF ALASKA’S SIX INITIATIVES: (1) HEALTHY BEGINNINGS, WHICH STRENGTHENS MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH AS A FOUNDATION FOR HEALTHY FAMILIES; (2) HEALTH CARE ACCESS, WHICH EXPANDS AND SUSTAINS ESSENTIAL PRIMARY, BEHAVIORAL, ORAL, SPECIALTY, EMERGENCY, HOME AND COMMUNITY-BASED AND POST-ACUTE CARE HEALTH SERVICES ACROSS ALASKA’S RURAL COMMUNITIES; (3) HEALTHY COMMUNITIES, WHICH INVESTS IN ENHANCING ACCESS TO PREVENTIVE AND PRIMARY CARE SERVICES THAT ENABLE EARLY CHRONIC DISEASE MANAGEMENT, EXPANDING THE USE OF CONSUMER-FACING DIGITAL TOOLS AND POPULATION HEALTH CLINICAL INFRASTRUCTURE, AND PROMOTING HEALTHY LIFESTYLES WITH CULTURALLY APPROPRIATE COMMUNITY EDUCATION; (4) PAY FOR VALUE: FISCAL SUSTAINABILITY, WHICH INCENTIVIZES A SHIFT FROM TRADITIONAL VOLUME-BASED REIMBURSEMENT MODELS TO BUILD THE LONG-TERM FINANCIAL STABILITY OF RURAL PROVIDERS THROUGH VOLUNTARY INNOVATIVE CARE AND PAYMENT MODELS THAT INCREASE CARE COORDINATION, LOWER COSTS AND IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES; (5) STRENGTHEN WORKFORCE, WHICH BUILDS A RESILIENT RURAL HEALTH CARE WORKFORCE THROUGH PIPELINE, RECRUITMENT, TRAINING AND RETENTION STRATEGIES, ALONGSIDE WRAPAROUND HOUSING AND CHILD CARE SUPPORTS TO HELP PROVIDERS REMAIN IN RURAL COMMUNITIES; AND (6) SPARK TECHNOLOGY AND INNOVATION, WHICH HARNESSES DATA AND TECHNOLOGY TO EXPAND THE USE OF CONSUMER WEARABLES AND DIGITAL DEVICES, ENHANCE TELEHEALTH, FOSTER APPROPRIATE USE OF AI, STRENGTHEN CYBERSECURITY, FACILITATE DATA SHARING AND SYSTEM INTEROPERABILITY, AND TEST NEW DELIVERY MODALITIES USING EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES. THESE SIX INITIATIVES ARE FLEXIBLE, PHASED, AND VOLUNTARY, ALLOWING EACH COMMUNITY AND PROVIDER TO ENGAGE AT A PACE AND SCALE SUITED TO THEIR LOCAL PRIORITIES AND RESOURCES. THESE INITIATIVES WILL TRANSFORM ALASKA’S HEALTH SYSTEM. THEY REFLECT ALASKA’S CULTURE OF INNOVATION AND SELF-RELIANCE, AND AFFIRM OUR COMMITMENT TO HIGH-QUALITY, ACCESSIBLE, AND SUSTAINABLE CARE.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
